An Anthropic mathematician claims to have proved the Riemann hypothesis with the help of Claude.

If verified, this would mark a major achievement for AI in advanced mathematics.

Here are the key technical developments I am tracking across the AI space today:

🧮 Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge reported using Claude to help prove the Riemann hypothesis, one of mathematics's most famous Millennium Prize problems.

📊 Baseten released bison-1 and groundhog-1, two open-weight decision models built on Gemma 4. Both support 128k context windows and image input, with bison-1 scoring 76 on the AA Decision Index v2.1.

⚡ Google expanded its lineup with Gemini 4 Neon—its fourth Gemini 4 model in five weeks after Argon, Carbon, and Hydrogen. Early tests evaluated Neon across seven real jobs against Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol.

🛡️ OpenAI outlined a multi-layered defense against adversarial distillation, combining model safeguards, detection, enforcement, and specialized training to protect against capability extraction.

🎨 Gemini can now execute multi-step creative chores on macOS, such as taking a child's butterfly sketch, modeling it, and rigging it inside Blender.

As models expand into decision-making, formal proofs, and desktop execution, defense strategies against capability extraction are becoming just as vital as raw performance.

Which of these updates holds the most potential for your engineering workflow?
